summary: Completed comprehensive testing of Task Templates feature. Backend: 23/23 tests passed. Frontend: All UI components verified via Playwright - Templates button visible, panel opens correctly, Create Template form has all required fields, Use Template dialog functional.

issues: Console warning: DialogContent missing Description or aria-describedby (non-blocking accessibility improvement)

endpoints_tested: GET /api/projects/templates - list templates with optional project_id filter
POST /api/projects/templates - create global or project-specific template
PUT /api/projects/templates/{id} - update template name, priority, recurring settings
POST /api/projects/templates/{id}/create-task - create task from template with overrides
verified_features: Templates can be Global (project_id=null) or Project-specific
Templates include checklist_items that are copied to created tasks
usage_count increments when task is created from template
Template supports recurring settings (is_recurring, recurrence_pattern, recurrence_interval)

elements_verified: Templates button visible on project detail page (data-testid='templates-btn')
Button click opens right-side Sheet panel
Panel shows 'Task Templates' header with BookCopy icon
Create Template button (rose color) at top of panel
Templates list shows existing 'Weekly Team Standup' template
Template card displays: name, scope (Global), description, priority badge, estimated hours, weekly indicator, checklist count (3 items), usage count
Dialog shows template name and description preview
Task Name input (pre-filled with template name, editable)

critical_code_review_comments: Backend template APIs follow REST conventions correctly with proper error handling (404 for not found)
Frontend TaskTemplatesPanel uses proper React state management with useState hooks
Sheet component from shadcn/ui provides good UX for side panel
Form validation is minimal - only name is required, which is appropriate for templates
Checklist items are properly serialized using model_dump() in backend
Usage count increment uses MongoDB $inc for atomicity
